The Daphnephoria; a triumphal procession held every ninth year at Thebes, in honour of Apollo, and to commemorate a victory of the Thebans over the M,olians of Arne. Its name was derived from the laurel branches carried by those who took part in the festival —the laurel, or more properly, the bay, being sacred to Apollo. The procession is led by a youthful priest called the Daphnephoros , before him a boy, his kinsman, bears a symbolic standard called the Kopo, and indicating the sun, moon, and stats.
